name: XNPV
description: XNPV returns the net present value of cash flows occurring at irregular intervals using a discount rate.
tldr: Calculates the net present value for a schedule of cash flows that is not necessarily periodic.

parameters.name: rate
parameters.description: Discount rate to apply to the cash flows.

parameters.name: values
parameters.description: Series of cash flows corresponding to the dates.

parameters.name: dates
parameters.description: Series of dates corresponding to the cash flows.

basicExample.explanation: A2:A5 contains dates and B2:B5 contains the cash flows, discounted at 10%.

advancedExamples.title: Include initial investment
advancedExamples.description: Initial investment is included in the values array on the first date
advancedExamples.explanation: Unlike NPV, XNPV includes the initial investment in the values array because it is tied to a date.

howItWorks: XNPV discounts each cash flow to the first date using the actual number of days between dates. The discount rate is annualized.

howToSteps.name: Calculate
howToSteps.text: Press Enter to get the result.

limitations: Dates must be valid and the values array must match the dates array in length.
The initial investment is included in the values array, not added separately.

commonErrors.cause: Dates and values arrays have different lengths or dates are invalid.
commonErrors.fix: Ensure arrays match and dates are valid.

commonErrors.cause: Initial investment was added outside the formula.
commonErrors.fix: Include the initial investment in the values array with its date.

googleSheetsEquivalent.description: XNPV works identically in Google Sheets.
googleSheetsEquivalent.notes: Same syntax and behavior as Excel.

faq.question: What is the difference between NPV and XNPV?
faq.answer: NPV assumes equal periods. XNPV uses actual dates for irregular intervals.

faq.question: Do I add the initial investment separately in XNPV?
faq.answer: No, include it in the values array with its date.
